cards.question: How are high-risk surgical patients identified preoperatively?
cards.answer: Combine clinical (frailty, METs <4, P-POSSUM), biochemical (NT-proBNP, troponin) and functional (CPET — anaerobic threshold <11 mL/kg/min, VO₂peak <15) measures; aggregate predicts 30-day mortality >5%.

cards.question: What is the evidence for goal-directed haemodynamic therapy?
cards.answer: Older meta-analyses suggested fewer complications, but the OPTIMISE trial itself was not significant (36.6% vs 43.4%, P=0.07) and the larger OPTIMISE II (2024, n=2,498) found no reduction in postoperative infection and more early arrhythmias with the inotrope protocol. Routine GDT is therefore not proven in modern enhanced-recovery care.

cards.question: When should postoperative ICU admission be offered?
cards.answer: After major surgery in patients with predicted mortality >5%, intra-operative instability requiring vasopressors >2 h, massive transfusion, persistent lactate >2 mmol/L, or unplanned organ support — per RCoA/AAGBI peri-operative care guidelines.
